review.translation: [And the waters|0] [were|1] [steadily|2] [receding|3] [until|4] [the|5] [tenth|6] [month|5]. [In the tenth|7] {month}, [on the first|8] [of the month|9], [the tops of|11] [the mountains|12] [became visible|10].

draft.change: Add Genesis 8:5 as verse evidence for the existing sense ‘a body or flow of water’ in mayim.
draft.definition: מַיִם can denote a body of water, here the floodwaters covering the land.
draft.evidence: In Genesis 8:5 the waters recede until the mountaintops become visible.

analysis.evidence: The plural verb הָיוּ agrees with הַמַּיִם. The predicate הָיוּ הָלוֹךְ וְחָסוֹר says the waters kept receding, and the appearance of the mountaintops shows what the floodwaters had covered.
analysis.morphology: וְ־ conjunction ‘and’ + הַ־ definite article, doubling the following מ + מַיִם masculine plural noun in the absolute state.
analysis.sense: a body or flow of water

analysis.evidence: הָיוּ agrees with the plural subject הַמַּיִם, “the waters.” The infinitives absolute הָלוֹךְ וְחָסוֹר express continued decrease. Together the clause means “the waters were steadily receding until the tenth month.”
analysis.morphology: Qal perfect, third person common plural, with no prefix or suffix pronoun
analysis.sense: to be, used as an auxiliary with an ongoing action

analysis.evidence: In הָיוּ הָלוֹךְ וְחָסוֹר, וְחָסוֹר expresses the decrease and הָלוֹךְ marks its continuation. The waters kept receding until the tenth month.

In וְהַמַּיִם הָיוּ הָלוֹךְ וְחָסוֹר, the waters are the subject. Paired with הָלוֹךְ, וְחָסוֹר describes their level continuing to fall. By the first day of the tenth month, the mountaintops were visible.
analysis.morphology: Qal infinitive absolute with prefixed conjunction וְ.
analysis.sense: to diminish in amount or level

analysis.evidence: עַד introduces הַחֹדֶשׁ הָעֲשִׂירִי, “the tenth month,” marking how long the waters continued to recede. The next clause dates the appearance of the mountaintops to the first day of that month.
analysis.morphology: Simple preposition with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: The ordinal הָעֲשִׂירִי modifies הַחֹדֶשׁ in עַד הַחֹדֶשׁ הָעֲשִׂירִי, “until the tenth month.” The following date specifies the first day of that month.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular absolute noun with prefixed definite article הַ־.

analysis.evidence: In עַד הַחֹדֶשׁ הָעֲשִׂירִי, “until the tenth month,” הָעֲשִׂירִי agrees with הַחֹדֶשׁ in gender, number, and definiteness and gives the month’s position in sequence.
analysis.morphology: Ordinal adjective, masculine singular absolute, with the prefixed definite article הָ־.

analysis.evidence: בָּעֲשִׂירִי repeats the ordinal from הַחֹדֶשׁ הָעֲשִׂירִי, leaving חֹדֶשׁ understood. The following בְּאֶחָד לַחֹדֶשׁ specifies the first day of that month.
analysis.morphology: Ordinal adjective, masculine singular absolute, with prefixed בְּ and the definite article, used substantivally.

analysis.evidence: בָּעֲשִׂירִי identifies the tenth month, and בְּאֶחָד לַחֹדֶשׁ specifies the day when the mountaintops appeared. In this date formula, אֶחָד denotes the first day of the month.
analysis.morphology: Preposition בְּ prefixed to a masculine singular absolute cardinal numeral used ordinally.
analysis.sense: first (in a count, and of dates)

analysis.evidence: הַחֹדֶשׁ הָעֲשִׂירִי identifies the tenth month. בְּאֶחָד לַחֹדֶשׁ gives the day within it, “on the first day of the month,” when the mountaintops became visible.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular absolute noun with prefixed preposition לְ and definite article, combined as לַ.

analysis.evidence: The plural verb נִרְאוּ agrees with its subject רָאשֵׁי הֶהָרִים, “the mountaintops.” As the waters receded, the mountaintops came into view.
analysis.morphology: Niphal perfect, third person common plural

analysis.evidence: רָאשֵׁי הֶהָרִים means “the summits of the mountains.” As the floodwaters receded, these highest parts became visible (נִרְאוּ).
analysis.morphology: Masculine plural construct form of the common noun רֹאשׁ, followed by הֶהָרִים (“the mountains”).

analysis.evidence: In נִרְאוּ רָאשֵׁי הֶהָרִים, “the tops of the mountains became visible,” רָאשֵׁי is in the construct state and הֶהָרִים names the mountains whose peaks emerged as the floodwaters receded.
analysis.morphology: Masculine plural absolute noun with the prefixed definite article הֶ־.
